subject: Banking
title: Banking APIs and Open Finance
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Banking APIs and Open Finance.

hook.text: APIs let apps talk to bank systems. Your budget app reads your bank data because an API connects them securely.

buildup.text: Europe's PSD2 regulation forced banks to open APIs. Third parties can access account data with customer consent.

discovery.text: Open banking spawned thousands of fintech apps. Lending, budgeting, investing, and payments all built on bank APIs.

twist.text: Banks fought open banking because it lets competitors access their customers.

climax.text: Open banking shifted power from banks to customers. Your data, your choice of who sees it and what they build with it.

punchline.text: Banks forced to share data. Customers gained choice. Fintech exploded.

quiz.question: What did Europe's PSD2 regulation require?
options: Banks to open APIs for third-party access with customer consent

details.summary: Banking APIs allow third-party apps to access bank account data and initiate payments with customer permission, creating an ecosystem where fintech companies can build services on top of traditional bank infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: Open banking APIs are dismantling the banks' monopoly on customer financial data. By letting competitors access account information, regulators are forcing competition and innovation in financial services.
takeaways: The EU's PSD2 directive mandated banks open APIs to third parties
Open banking enables account aggregation, automated switching, and comparison tools
Banks initially resisted but now see APIs as a competitive advantage

faq.question: Is open banking safe for consumers?
faq.answer: Open banking requires explicit customer consent and uses strong authentication. Data access is read-only unless the customer authorizes payment initiation. Regulated third parties must meet the same security standards as banks.

faq.question: How do banking APIs benefit consumers?
faq.answer: They allow apps to aggregate all your accounts in one view, automatically find better rates, initiate payments without logging into each bank, and provide personalized financial insights based on your actual spending data.
